description: A common fungal leaf disease of maize worldwide. It causes long cigar-shaped lesions on leaves that reduce photosynthesis and can lead to major yield losses.
symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on lower leaves
Gray-green lesions that later turn tan or brown
Dark fungal sporulation in mature lesions
Large blighted leaf areas when lesions merge
Severe infections can kill entire leaves or plants
visual_symptoms: long cigar-shaped lesions on maize leaves
tan or gray leaf spots with dark centers
large dead areas on infected leaves
spread: Rain splash spreading spores between plants
Survival of fungus on infected leaf debris
impact: Severe outbreaks may cause up to 70% yield loss
management: Plant resistant or tolerant maize hybrids
Rotate maize with non-host crops such as soybean or sunflower
Scout fields regularly for early symptoms
Apply fungicides when first lesions appear below the ear leaf
biological_control: Encouraging beneficial microbes in soil may reduce pathogen survival
chemical_control: Foliar fungicides such as strobilurin or triazole fungicides
Apply fungicides when first lesions appear
Follow regional recommendations for maize disease control
prevention: Deep ploughing or residue management to reduce inoculum
Monitor fields during humid weather conditions
source: Plant pathology literature on maize diseases
